problem: Börschinger et al. (2011)'s unsupervised PCFG induction for grounded language learning works only when each sentence has a small set of candidate meanings (e.g. sportscasting) and does not scale to the navigation instruction following task of Chen and Mooney (2011), where the space of potential meanings per sentence is very large.
motivation: Grounded language learning uses sentences paired with ambiguous perceptual contexts. Real navigation data gives highly ambiguous supervision, so the PCFG-based approach needs to be made scalable to be useful there.
key_idea: Enhance the unsupervised PCFG induction approach for grounded language learning so that it scales to highly ambiguous supervision, as in navigation instruction following.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so the mechanism and ablations are not visible. The abstract claims the enhancement makes PCFG induction tractable and effective where the earlier approach failed on the navigation task with large candidate meaning sets.
method: Unsupervised PCFG induction: builds on Börschinger et al. (2011) to learn a grammar mapping sentences to meaning representations from ambiguous context.
Scalability enhancement: modifies the PCFG construction to handle a large set of potential meanings per sentence (details not given in the abstract).

setting.backbone: Unsupervised PCFG induction (probabilistic grammar, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Navigation instruction data of Chen and Mooney (2011): instructions paired with ambiguous perceptual contexts (paths/action sequences)
setting.observation: Ambiguous perceptual context in a simulated virtual environment (not detailed in abstract)
setting.simulator: Chen and Mooney (2011) virtual-world navigation domain

results: The abstract reports that experiments on the navigation task demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, with no numbers given. It claims the enhanced PCFG method scales to highly ambiguous supervision where Börschinger et al. (2011) does not.
limitations: Abstract only; details and quantitative results not available.
Symbolic grammar-based approach in a simulated, restricted navigation domain.
